Subject: Observability: on‑prem forwarder authN + SIEM field mapping

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the initial onboarding last week. As we prep our private deployment, the security team needs a short, concrete plan for how Redwood's on‑prem forwarder will authenticate to our SIEM ingest (Splunk HEC) and how logs/traces will preserve chain of custody. High level asks:

- Recommended authN: do you want us to run a client cert (mTLS) or token? How do we rotate/automate?
- If we use mTLS, what tooling do you expect on our side (Vault, ACME, in‑house PKI)?
- Field mapping: we need a mapping doc for Splunk index/event fields (user identifiers, request_id, model_id, region).
- Tracing hooks: how do you recommend we propagate trace context from our app gateway through the forwarder into Redwood's tracing pipeline?
- Evidence/acceptance: security will require an evidence bundle (signed receipt of transferred logs, retention proof) — can you outline what Redwood can provide?

Do you have a short pre‑read or checklist we can share with our compliance team? Also available next Tue/Wed for a 45min workshop to walk through the plan.

Thanks,
Anna Brooks
Director, Cloud Operations | Nimbus Financial
anna.brooks@nimbusfin.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Observability: on‑prem forwarder authN + SIEM field mapping

Hi Anna — great to hear from you and glad the onboarding is moving. Below is a concise recommendation and what we can deliver as evidence. I've also attached a short architecture diagram and an acceptance checklist (see attachments).

1) Recommended authN model (primary): mTLS with short‑lived client certs issued from customer PKI (preferred flow)
   - Flow: your PKI issues client cert to the forwarder (or a fleet identity provider). Forwarder authenticates to Splunk HEC over TLS mutual auth.
   - Rotation: support short TTL certs (7–30 days). We recommend using HashiCorp Vault (recommended) or your ACME service. Redwood supports automatic cert reload without restarts.

2) Token fallback (secondary): if using HEC tokens, enforce per‑forwarder tokens with IP restrictions + HMAC signing for payloads. Tokens are acceptable for short pilots but will have weaker chain‑of‑custody guarantees.

3) Field mapping / SIEM schema
   - We will provide a mapping file that maps: request_id -> event.request_id, model_id -> event.model_id, org_id ->metadata.org, redwood_node -> host.device, latency_ms -> metrics.latency_ms.
   - We also recommend injecting a signed 'transfer_id' header on every batch so the receipt can be validated later.

4) Tracing hooks
   - Propagate W3C traceparent through the forwarder. Forwarder will preserve headers and emit trace spans to the tracing cluster with a dedicated tag redwood.deployment=nimbus-onprem.
   - For RPC bridging (if you use a gateway), add an explicit span tag event.request_source so traces are joinable on our side.

5) Evidence & acceptance
   - Redwood can provide: signed receipt logs (SHA256 of batched payloads with RFC‑3339 timestamp), forwarding delivery receipts, and per‑day delivery manifest.
   - Acceptance criteria (suggested): successful 48‑hour ingest with receipts, PASS on schema validation run against a 7‑day sample, and ability to query by transfer_id within 24 hours. See attached checklist.

Workshop: Tue Oct 12 10:00–10:45 PT or Wed Oct 13 11:00–11:45 PT. Which works?

Im copying Jonas (tracing) and Diego (SIEM mapping) to confirm technical details below.

Best,
Kimberly Park
